sections.content:
UK software engineering pay in 2026 shows a sharp split between London and the rest of the country. The national average sits around £55,000 per year, with Glassdoor reporting roughly £56,279 across tens of thousands of submissions and a typical range from £40,900 at the 25th percentile to £80,400 at the 75th.

That single number hides enormous regional variation. London averages around £68,000 across all seniority levels, while Manchester sits near £45,000 despite similar roles. Where you work, and who you work for, matter as much as how long you have been coding.
sections.title: Average Software Engineer Pay in the UK for 2026

sections.content:
Juniors with zero to two years of experience earn roughly £30,000 to £35,000 nationally, with London juniors averaging near £35,000 and Manchester or Birmingham juniors closer to £28,000 to £30,000. Mid-level engineers with three to five years earn around £52,000 nationally, rising to £55,000 to £80,000 in London.

Seniors with six or more years average £70,000 to £85,000 nationally, with London seniors at £85,000 to £115,000 in base pay. Staff and principal engineers in London reach £120,000 to £150,000 in base salary, and October 2026 benchmarks put senior total compensation between £100,000 and £183,000 from the 25th to the 75th percentile.
sections.title: Salary by Experience Level

sections.content:
London is the UK's highest-paying city at about £68,000 on average, followed by Cambridge near £55,000 and Edinburgh near £50,000. Manchester averages around £45,000, Bristol about £44,000, and Birmingham, Leeds and Sheffield trail further at a 30 to 35 percent discount to London.

Remote work has started to narrow the gap: a Manchester senior earning £65,000 locally can often negotiate £80,000 to £90,000 working remotely for a London fintech. Higher London pay still comes with much higher housing costs, so the real-terms comparison is closer than the headline figures suggest.
sections.title: London vs Regional Cities

sections.content:
Big Tech sets the ceiling for UK engineering pay: average total compensation at Google London runs near £171,000, Meta near £150,000 and Amazon around £124,000. Banks and fintech firms compete hard too, with senior base salaries of £90,000 to £140,000 and total compensation of £120,000 to over £200,000 once bonuses land.

Hedge funds and prop trading firms pay on another level entirely, with associate-level engineers clearing £120,000 to £250,000 in total comp and vice presidents reaching £350,000 to £700,000. AI, platform and security specialists command premiums above the general market at nearly every employer tier.
